# Rule B2: Powergaming Guidelines
[bold]Powergaming[/bold] is the act of prioritizing mechanics over roleplay for advantages in gameplay. Our focus here is to tell a story, part of that is being vulnerable, accepting a loss and not being good at everything. This allows a narrative to advance.
### Anti-Powergaming Behavior These are just a few measures to be followed that aids in preventing Powergaming: - [bold]Roleplay and engage with players if they’re attempting to roleplay a combat/antagonist/hostile scene[/bold]. If they’re emoting aiming a gun, or handling a hostage situation, do not immediately attack them mechanically whilst they’re mid roleplay. -- Leeway is given if the scene is near to a close, but all players are expected to engage with it in good faith; even if this puts you at a disadvantage. - [bold]Fear the Reaper[/bold]. In the Zekke Sector, most people are expected to be survivalists, so your character should naturally fear death. - [bold]Avoid restricting more personal CGP/Outlaw Gear[/bold]. This means do not take CGP/Outlaw encryption keys, and do not use their uplinks to purchase stuff if you are not of their respective faction. -- This does not disallow you from using other gear from the CGP/Outlaw pool, like the Breaching Hammer.
## Rule B2.1: Metagrudging [bold]Metagrudging[/bold] is a stronger form of Powergaming. It involves taking IC matters into OOC, and holding a grudge against a player between characters and shifts.
- [bold]Metagrudging does NOT mean your character can't hold a grudge against another character[/bold]. You can build relationships and rivalries as you see fit, so long as it exists only between those two characters. - [bold]Metagrudging isn't always violent or intended[/bold]. While in many cases you may have a hatred for the way someone plays the character, the metagrudge could just come from pre-existing actions that might've annoyed you before, or they could even come from loving a character too much beyond another character's connection. -- An example of this would be not wanting the local shopkeep to be hurt or crimed just because they are extremely endearing, without having met them.
### Tips to Avoid Metagrudging - [bold]Take breaks[/bold]. It's easy to get emotionally attached to characters if you play for long hours, so try to take time to handle things outside of the game as well. - [bold]Breathe[/bold]. Understand that it's okay to step away from an engagement if you are not having fun. Don't bottle it up to a point it becomes resentment; use LOOC/ShipOOC to communicate with other players if you're not having fun. - [bold]Avoid conflict[/bold]. You are allowed to pick and choose your engagements, within reason. If you don't want to mingle with a specific character, you can always use LOOC or ShipOOC to express your aversion. -- This does not mean you can't act in Outlaw/CGP activities without consequence, but impact can always be limited to a minimum to avoid as much interaction as possible.
## Rule B2.2: Omniships An [bold]Omniship[/bold] is a ship that attempts to perform all of the tasks that every Department handles. To avoid an Omniship: - [bold]Try to keep your ship to the Role/Departments it comes with[/bold]. If it lacks something, collaborate with other ships. Talk with them to get assistance with what you need. -- For reference, a ship is allowed two Roles and Four Subdepartments before it is classified as an Omniship. [italic](Check our Ship Submission guidelines for more info.)[/italic] -- Larger ships have more leniency, so long as you consistently have an active crew handling it and engage with other players. - [bold]Do not build ship thrusters inside of your ship[/bold]. They are expected to be external to space.
[italic](NOTE: This rule is intended in spirit. While it is loosely enforced, if we see egregious examples of Omniships, we will take action.)[/italic]
